{{Quote|Much later it was learned that they had reached the planet Naboo in the Wild Space of the southern galactic quadrant, where the colonists became embroiled in a war with the planet's native Gungans.|[[Historical Council]] of the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances]] describing the colonization of Naboo|<ref name="TNEC" />}}
Violent '''conflicts''' were fought between [[Human/Legends|Human]] [[Grizmallti/Legends|Grizmallti]] [[Colonist/Legends|colonists]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] and its native [[Gungan/Legends|Gungans]] in the [[Standard decade/Legends|decades]] following the landing of the colonists in approximately [[3900 BBY/Legends|3900 BBY]]. The conflicts ended with a non-aggression treaty in which both sides agreed to avoid each other. Tensions between the Humans, who came to call themselves the [[Naboo (people)/Legends|Naboo]], and the Gungans continued until the two socities were united during the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]] in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]].

==Prelude==
[[File:Naboo_planet.png|thumb|right|250px|Naboo was inhabited by Gungans prior to the arrival of humanity.]]
The [[Amphibian/Legends|amphibious]] [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]] [[Species/Legends|species]] was believed to be indigenous to the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]] [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]], which was untouched by [[Human/Legends|Humans]] until around [[4000 BBY/Legends|4000 BBY]]. Members of the [[Grizmallti/Legends|Grizmallti]], the Human inhabitants of<ref name="Nexus" /> the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]]<ref name="TEA" /> planet [[Grizmallt/Legends|Grizmallt]], discovered Naboo, which was then used as a vacation spot by Grizmallti aristocrats and as a hunting preserve. This caused the Gungans to withdraw into their world's [[Water/Legends|lakes]] and [[Swamp/Legends|swamps]] to keep to themselves.<ref name="Nexus" />

In approximately [[3900 BBY/Legends|3900 BBY]], [[Colonist/Legends|colonists]] from Grizmallt fled a [[Grizmallti civil war/Legends|civil war]] on their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] aboard a trio of [[Colony ship/Legends|colony ships]]: ''[[Beneficent Tasia]]'', ''[[Constant]]'', and ''[[Mother Vima]]''.<ref name="TNEC" /> Led by the [[Scout/Legends|scout]] [[Kwilaan/Legends|Kwilaan]],<ref name="Secrets">''[[Secrets of Naboo]]''</ref> they lost contact with their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] and landed on Naboo,<ref name="TNEC" /> although one of their [[Starship/Legends|ships]] crashed<ref name="Clone Wars">{{SW|url=explore/the-clone-wars/ep418|text="Crisis on Naboo" - ''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide|nolive=1}}"</ref> and the ''Beneficent Tasia'' was unable to contact Grizmallt. Within [[Standard week/Legends|weeks]] of their arrival, the Grizmallti encountered the Gungans.<ref name="GB">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]''</ref>

==The conflicts==
The Humans were warlike and initiated many of the conflicts between themselves and the Gungans,<ref name="EGTAS">[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species (real-world book)|''The Essential Guide to Alien Species'']]</ref> who united their clans in response to the new arrivals.<ref name="UAA">''[[Ultimate Alien Anthology]]''</ref> Despite their best efforts, [[Diplomat/Legends|diplomats]] on both sides failed to negotiate peace, and the Gungans and Humans fought brutal conflicts for territory and access to resources in the following [[Standard decade/Legends|decades]].<ref name="Nexus" /> In response to the unwanted presence of the Humans, the Gungans developed their own dialect of [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic Standard]] called [[Gungan (language)|Gunganese]] which served as a protest against the colonizers while also opening up communication with them. Due to their ability to communicate,<ref name="EGTAS" /> the two species eventually signed a peace treaty<ref name="Fact24">{{FactFile|24|NAB 1-4|Naboo}}</ref> in which both sides agreed to avoid each other while maintaining an intense distrust.<ref name="Nexus" />

==Aftermath==
[[File:Gungan_society.png|thumb|left|300px|The Gungan species dwelt in their underwater cities following the conflict.]]
As a result of the conflict, the Humans reinvented their culture to focus on peace, art, and knowledge, also calling themselves the [[Naboo (people)/Legends|Naboo]]. The Gungans abandoned their surface settlements and retreated to their underwater [[City/Legends|cities]]<ref name="Secrets" /> where they discovered [[Locap/Legends|locap]], a [[Plant/Legends|plant]] from which they could extract [[Plasma/Legends|plasma]] to use as an energy source. This allowed them to maintain their underwater settlements permanently.<ref name="Inside">''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars: Episode I]]''</ref> The following generations of Gungans would occasionally return to the ruins of their surface cities in what [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] sociologists speculated were religious rituals.<ref name="Secrets" /> Both civilizations eventually had their own civil wars, with the Gungan tribes [[War of the Gungan tribes|warring]] with each other in [[3000 BBY]] and the Naboo entering the [[Time of Suffering/Legends|Time of Suffering]]<ref name="TEA" /> from approximately [[1032 BBY/Legends|1032 BBY]] to [[832 BBY/Legends|832 BBY]].<ref name="Nexus" />

The animosity between the Humans and Gungans persisted for generations,<ref name="Fact24" /> although some Gungans reluctantly traded with the Naboo.<ref name="UAA" /> Another [[Gungan–Naboo War|war]] between the Gungans and the Naboo occurred in approximately [[127 BBY]] or [[125 BBY]], in which Naboo's [[Unidentified Queen of Naboo (Gungan–Naboo War)|queen]] was [[Death/Legends|killed]].<ref name="Darth Plageuis">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref> Both species later united under the leadership of [[Monarch of Naboo/Legends|Queen]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]] of the Naboo and [[Boss/Legends|Boss]] [[Rugor Nass/Legends|Rugor Nass]] of the Gungans to repel the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] in the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]]<ref name="Fact24" /> in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]].<ref name="TNEC" /> 

''[[The Essential Guide to Alien Species]]'', a work adapted by a [[Ann Margaret Lewis|writer]] from the notes of [[Senior Anthropologist]] [[Mammon Hoole]] and published during or after [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]], referenced the conflicts and their impact on the Gungan language.<ref name="EGTAS" /> An updated version of the [[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species (book)|guide]] published during or after [[36 ABY]] stated that there were no historical records of armed conflict between Humans and Gungans, instead attributing the conflict between the species to communication difficulties.<ref name="NEGTAS">''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''</ref> The war between the Humans and Gungans was mentioned in a [[The New Essential Chronology (in-universe)|chronicle]] of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] compiled by the [[Galactic Federation of Free Alliances|Galactic Alliance]] [[Historical Council]] in 36 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|ABY]].<ref name="TNEC" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|Although we do not always agree, your honor, our two great societies have always lived in peace.|Padmé Amidala, seemingly refuting the existence of the war between Humans and Gungans|<ref name="TPM">{{Film|I}}</ref>}}
[[File:Amidala_reveals_identity.png|thumb|right|300px|Padmé Amidala (front) claims that the Naboo and Gungans have always lived in peace in ''The Phantom Menace''.]]
The conflict that forced the Gungans to live underwater was first mentioned in ''[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars: Episode I]]'', a reference book by [[Kristin Lund]] published in [[2000]].<ref name="Inside" /> The conflict was established to have been between the Gungans and the Humans in ''[[Secrets of Naboo]]'', a [[2001]] sourcebook for the [[Wizards of the Coast]] ''[[Star Wars Roleplaying Game]]''.<ref name="Secrets" /> A variety of sources suggest that no war between the Gungans and the Humans ever took place. In the [[1999]] [[prequel trilogy]] film [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'' Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']], Queen Padmé Amidala states that both Gungan and Naboo societies had lived in peace.<ref name="TPM" /> The [[2015]] sourcebook ''[[Nexus of Power]]'', published by [[Fantasy Flight Games]] for use with the ''[[Star Wars: Force and Destiny]]'' roleplaying game, suggested that the Human colonists did not refer to themselves as the Naboo until after their conflict with the Gungans.<ref name="Nexus" />

The [[Databank (original)|Databank]] on [[StarWars.com]] also specified that the Gungans and Naboo had never been at war.<ref name="Gungan databank">{{DB|species|gungan|Gungan}}</ref> Another source to refute the existence of the conflicts was the DataBank in the 2001 [[LucasArts]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]'', which stated that neither Humans or Gungans attacked each other and instead maintained a tense relationship.<ref name="GB" /> Additionally, during the game's development, early levels of the Gungan campaign were intended to involve a conflict between the Gungan [[Boss/Legends|Boss]] [[Gallo/Legends|Gallo]] and Human Naboo tyrants, but the members of the creative team, including level designer [[Stephen J. McManus]], were informed that [[canon]]ically no war between the two civilizations had taken place. McManus therefore redesigned the campaign to become a war between Gungans.<ref name="GBBTS">{{LucasArts|url=products/battlegrounds/diaries3.htm|text=Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds - Designer Diary #3}}</ref>

In [[2004]], ''[[Star Wars Galaxies: Jump to Lightspeed: Prima Official Game Guide]]'' stated that the Humans and Gungans did not attack each other despite their opposition, but acknowledged that armed clashes were rare.<ref name="Galaxies">[[Star Wars Galaxies: Jump to Lightspeed: Prima Official Game Guide|''Star Wars Galaxies: Jump to Lightspeed'': Prima Official Game Guide]]</ref> The [[2006]] reference book ''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]'' by [[Ann Margaret Lewis (real person)|Ann Margaret Lewis]], styled as a partially [[in-universe]] guide, states that there were no historical records of armed conflict between the species.<ref name="NEGTAS" /> [[2008]]'s ''[[Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide]]'' also described the Gungans as "unperturbed" by the arrival of Humans.<ref name="Kotor">''[[Knights of the Old Republic Campaign Guide]]''</ref> This article follows sources that establish that the conflicts occurred.

The entry for the Naboo people in ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' states that a war occurred several centuries before the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|Battle of Naboo]] in which large numbers of Naboo and Gungans were killed, which lead to the realization that they could not survive independently and the establishment of trading relationships. However, this could be referring to the later [[Gungan–Naboo War|war]] between them or the [[Gungan-mercenary war|war]] between the Gungans and a group of mercenaries.<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|II|353|Naboo, the}}</ref>
